passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following management's discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations ("MD&A") should be read together with our audited consolidated financial statements and notes thereto, which are included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. We utilize a 52-53 week fiscal year ending on the Saturday closest to March 31. As such, Fiscal 2026 ended on March 28, 2026 and was a 52-week period; Fiscal 2025 ended on March 29, 2025 and was a 52-week period; Fiscal 2024 ended on March 30, 2024 and was a 52-week period; and Fiscal 2027 will end on April 3, 2027 and will be a 53-week period. INTRODUCTION MD&A is provided as a supplement to the accompanying consolidated financial statements and notes thereto to help provide an understanding of our results of operations, financial condition, and liquidity. MD&A is organized as follows: • Overview. This section provides a general description of our business, global economic conditions and industry trends, and a summary of our financial performance for Fiscal 2026. In addition, this section includes a discussion of recent developments and transactions affecting comparability that we believe are important in understanding our results of operations and financial condition, and in anticipating future trends. • Results of operations. This section provides an analysis of our results of operations for Fiscal 2026 compared to Fiscal 2025. • Financial condition and liquidity. This section provides a discussion of our financial condition and liquidity as of March 28, 2026, which includes (i) an analysis of our financial condition as compared to the prior fiscal year-end; (ii) an analysis of changes in our cash flows for Fiscal 2026 compared to the prior fiscal year; (iii) an analysis of our liquidity, including the availability under our commercial paper borrowing program and credit facilities, our supplier finance program, outstanding debt and covenant compliance, common stock repurchases, and payments of dividends; and (iv) a summary of our material cash requirements as of March 28, 2026. • Market risk management. This section discusses how we manage our risk exposures related to foreign currency exchange rates, interest rates, and our investments as of March 28, 2026. • Critical accounting policies. This section discusses our critical accounting policies considered to be important to our results of operations and financial condition, which typically require significant judgment and estimation on the part of management in their application. In addition, all of our significant accounting policies, including our critical accounting policies, are summarized in Note 3 to the accompanying consolidated financial statements. • Recently issued accounting standards. This section discusses the potential impact on our reported results of operations and financial condition of certain accounting standards that have been recently issued. For discussion related to the results of operations and changes in our cash flows for Fiscal 2025 compared to Fiscal 2024, refer to Part II, Item 7. " Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations " in our Fiscal 2025 Form 10-K. OVERVIEW

Summary of Financial Performance Operating Results In Fiscal 2026, we reported net revenues of $8.115 billion, net income of $941.1 million, and net income per diluted share of $15.11, as compared to net revenues of $7.079 billion, net income of $742.9 million, and net income per diluted share of $11.61 in Fiscal 2025. The comparability of our operating results has been affected by net restructuring-related charges, and certain other charges, as well as foreign currency volatility. Our operating results are also susceptible to changes in macroeconomic conditions. Our operating performance for Fiscal 2026 reflected revenue increases of 14.6% on a reported basis and 11.8% on a constant currency basis, as defined within " Transactions and Trends Affecting Comparability of Results of Operations and Financial Condition " below. Net revenues reflected growth across all of our reportable segments. Our gross profit as a percentage of net revenues increased by 130 basis points to 69.9% during Fiscal 2026, primarily driven by average unit retail ("AUR") growth, product elevation, and favorable foreign currency effects, more than offsetting pressure from tariffs and non-cotton product costs. Selling, general, and administrative ("SG&A") expenses as a percentage of net revenues decreased by 70 basis points to 53.9% during Fiscal 2026, largely attributable to operating leverage on higher net revenues despite higher compensation-related expenses, marketing investments, and variable selling expenses. Net income increased by $198.2 million to $941.1 million in Fiscal 2026 as compared to Fiscal 2025, primarily due to a $247.1 million increase in our operating income, partially offset by a $28.8 million increase in our income tax provision and a $20.1 million increase in our non-operating expense, net. Net income per diluted share increased by $3.50 to $15.11 per share during Fiscal 2026 driven by the higher level of net income and lower weighted-average diluted shares outstanding. During Fiscal 2026 and Fiscal 2025, our operating results were negatively impacted by net restructuring-related charges and certain other charges totaling $118.1 million and $57.8 million, respectively, which had an after-tax effect of reducing net income by $92.1 million, or $1.48 per diluted share, and $46.0 million, or $0.72 per diluted share, respectively. Financial Condition and Liquidity We ended Fiscal 2026 in a net cash and short-term investments position (calculated as cash and cash equivalents, plus short-term investments, less total debt) of $826.1 million, as compared to $940.4 million as of the end of Fiscal 2025. The decrease in our net cash and short-term investments position at March 28, 2026 as compared to March 29, 2025 was primarily due to our use of cash to support Class A common stock repurchases of $623.8 million, including withholdings in satisfaction of tax obligations for stock-based compensation awards, to invest in our business through $408.1 million in capital expenditures, and to make dividend payments of $216.5 million, partially offset by our operating cash flows of $1.154 billion. credit_strengths.text: RL's revenue and operating income have grown steadily over the past three fiscal years, with operating margin now above the sector median, reflecting successful product elevation and pricing power. This consistent top-line expansion and margin improvement support the issuer's ability to generate internal funds for debt service and shareholder returns.

The company maintains a net cash position, with cash and short-term investments exceeding total debt, and a current ratio well above the sector median. This liquidity buffer, combined with robust operating cash flow, provides substantial financial flexibility and a cushion against cyclical demand or unexpected cash needs.

key_risks.text: RL's operating results are susceptible to macroeconomic conditions and foreign currency volatility, as disclosed in the risk factors. Revenue growth could stall if consumer discretionary spending weakens or currency headwinds intensify, pressuring margins and cash flow generation. This cyclical exposure is a key credit risk despite current strength.

The company's debt structure includes a mix of long-term and short-term borrowings, with total debt increasing over the past year. While no specific maturity profile is disclosed, the reliance on commercial paper and credit facilities introduces refinancing risk. A deterioration in credit markets could impair access to these funding sources.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is exceptionally strong, with operating income covering interest expense more than twenty times, far exceeding the sector median. This ample coverage, combined with a net cash position, indicates that RL can easily service its debt obligations from current earnings, even under a moderate earnings decline.

Operating cash flow has been consistently robust, exceeding one billion dollars annually, and is more than sufficient to cover interest and principal repayments. However, capital expenditures are not available in the data, limiting our ability to assess free cash flow after investment. This data gap is material for evaluating cash flow adequacy.

overall_credit_view.text: RL exhibits a minimal indicative financial risk profile, characterized by net cash, high interest coverage, and strong operating margins relative to sector peers. The company's consistent revenue growth and cash generation support a stable credit outlook. We view the issuer as having ample capacity to meet its obligations.

However, shareholder distributions, including significant buybacks and dividends, absorb a large portion of operating cash flow, reducing financial flexibility. While this is manageable given the net cash position, a sustained increase in distributions or a downturn in operating performance could erode the liquidity cushion and weaken credit metrics over time.

credit_strengths.text: RL 的營業收入及經營溢利於過去三個財政年度穩步增長，經營利潤率現時高於行業中位數，反映產品升級及定價能力成功。此持續的營業額擴張及利潤率改善，支持發行人產生內部資金以償還債務及回饋股東的能力。
公司維持淨現金狀況，現金及短期投資超過總債務，流動比率遠高於行業中位數。此流動性緩衝，加上強勁的經營現金流，提供充裕的財務彈性及緩衝，以應對週期性需求或意外現金需求。

key_risks.text: 如風險因素所披露，RL 的經營業績易受宏觀經濟狀況及外匯波動影響。若消費者非必需支出減弱或貨幣逆風加劇，營業收入增長可能停滯，對利潤率及現金流產生構成壓力。儘管目前表現強勁，此週期性風險為關鍵信用風險。
公司的債務結構包括長期及短期借款組合，總債務於過去一年增加。儘管未披露具體到期情況，依賴商業票據及信貸融資帶來再融資風險。信貸市場惡化可能損害獲取該等資金來源的能力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率異常強勁，經營溢利覆蓋利息支出超過二十倍，遠超行業中位數。此充裕覆蓋，加上淨現金狀況，表明 RL 可輕鬆以當前盈利償還債務責任，即使盈利適度下降亦然。
經營現金流一直穩健，每年超過十億美元，足以覆蓋利息及本金還款。然而，數據中未提供資本支出，限制我們評估投資後自由現金流的能力。此數據缺口對評估現金流充足性屬重大。

overall_credit_view.text: RL 展現極低的指示性財務風險狀況，其特徵為淨現金、高利息覆蓋率及相對於行業同業的強勁經營利潤率。公司持續的營業收入增長及現金產生支持穩定的信用展望。我們認為發行人有充裕能力履行其責任。
然而，股東分派，包括重大回購及股息，佔用經營現金流的一大部分，降低財務彈性。儘管鑑於淨現金狀況此屬可管理，但分派持續增加或經營表現下滑可能隨時間侵蝕流動性緩衝並削弱信用指標。
